contests.title: Firebaugh fire and emergency-response parcel tax — Measure F

provenance.quote: To ensure 24/7 response to fires and medical emergencies such as heart attacks, strokes, and car accidents; hire/train firefighters/EMTs; upgrade safety equipment, vehicles/life-saving rescue tools, shall a measure be adopted to enact a $95/year parcel tax for single family homes and specified amounts for multifamily, commercial, agricultural, and industrial parcels, providing approximately $240,000/year until ended by voters; requiring independent oversight; funds used only for Firebaugh Fire Department response?

measures.questionText: To ensure 24/7 response to fires and medical emergencies such as heart attacks, strokes, and car accidents; hire/train firefighters/EMTs; upgrade safety equipment, vehicles/life-saving rescue tools, shall a measure be adopted to enact a $95/year parcel tax for single family homes and specified amounts for multifamily, commercial, agricultural, and industrial parcels, providing approximately $240,000/year until ended by voters; requiring independent oversight; funds used only for Firebaugh Fire Department response?

provenance.quote: To ensure 24/7 response to fires and medical emergencies such as heart attacks, strokes, and car accidents; hire/train firefighters/EMTs; upgrade safety equipment, vehicles/life-saving rescue tools, shall a measure be adopted to enact a $95/year parcel tax for single family homes and specified amounts for multifamily, commercial, agricultural, and industrial parcels, providing approximately $240,000/year until ended by voters; requiring independent oversight; funds used only for Firebaugh Fire Department response?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Creates an ongoing tax on Firebaugh property to fund fire and emergency response, starting at $95 a year for a single-family parcel, with different charges for multifamily, agricultural, commercial and industrial property. It has no scheduled expiration and is estimated to raise $240,000 a year.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the specified parcel-tax rates, legally restricted fire and emergency-response uses, exemptions, independent citizen oversight and annual public reporting.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not create this new fire and emergency-response parcel tax.

parts.label: Rates by property category
parts.what: The ordinance sets maximum annual charges of $95 per single-family residential parcel, $65 per multifamily residential unit, $95 per acre of agricultural property, $495 per commercial parcel and $750 per industrial parcel. Categories follow zoning. The agricultural per-acre rule is explicit in the ordinance; the shorter analysis describes it as per parcel.

parts.label: Restricted services and equipment
parts.what: Proceeds must go into a special fund for Council-approved fire and emergency services. Authorized uses include firefighting and emergency-medical equipment, rescue tools, vehicles, protective gear, communications and other response resources, and paid around-the-clock emergency shift coverage.

parts.label: Exemptions and parcel records
parts.what: Government/public-agency property and property specifically exempt under applicable state or federal law are exempt. Private owners seeking a legal exemption must submit the City’s proof form before June 30 preceding the first fiscal year requested. County assessor records as of March 1 determine the next year’s parcel calculation. The tax is not based on property value.

parts.label: Citizen committee and public reporting
parts.what: A five-member unpaid committee of City residents must independently review spending and report to the Council. Members are nominated by the Manager and approved by Council, serve two-year terms with at most two consecutive terms, and meet at least twice annually. The annual receipts-and-spending report is due January 31 after each fiscal year. The City Attorney’s analysis also describes financial audits. Terms expire May 1; members continue until a successor is appointed and confirmed.

parts.label: Administration, appeals and collection
parts.what: The City Manager or designee administers the tax. Determinations may be appealed in writing within 30 days; Council must issue its decision by June 30 before the levy year. Collection follows county property-tax dates, penalties and interest, and unpaid amounts become a parcel lien and personal obligation of the owner when due.

parts.label: Approval, start and duration
parts.what: At least two-thirds of votes cast must approve Measure F. It takes effect ten days after Council declares the result and continues indefinitely unless voters repeal it. If a court invalidates part of the ordinance, remaining provisions continue as far as the law allows.
